assertion_results.text: The plan uses Rust's idiomatic null guard patterns for each field — unwrap_or_default(), as_ref(), map(), or if-let/match — rather than calling .unwrap() directly
assertion_results.evidence: In plan.md lines 42-58, the extract_vulnerability_summary method uses: cves -> `.as_ref().cloned().unwrap_or_default()`, affected_packages -> `.as_ref().map(|pkgs| pkgs.len() as u32).unwrap_or(0)`, severity_counts -> `.as_ref().cloned().unwrap_or_default()`. No `.unwrap()` calls appear anywhere in the plan. null-guards.md line 105-107 explicitly states: 'Every `Option<T>` field is unwrapped with a fallback, never with `.unwrap()` or `.expect()`'.

assertion_results.text: The plan does NOT access any of the three Option fields without a guard — no direct .len(), .join(), or iteration on Option<T> without unwrapping safely
assertion_results.evidence: In plan.md lines 42-58: cves is unwrapped via unwrap_or_default() before .len() is called on the resulting Vec (line 46: 'let cve_count = cve_list.len() as u32'). affected_packages uses .map(|pkgs| pkgs.len()) where .len() is called inside the map closure on the inner Vec, not on the Option. severity_counts is unwrapped via unwrap_or_default() before any access. No direct .len(), .join(), or iteration on any Option<T>.
